questions.statement: Choose the sentence that correctly uses the present perfect.
questions.context: Practica de presente perfecto, Lima, grado 11.

options.text: I have visited Cusco twice.
options.feedback: Auxiliary 'have' plus past participle is the correct structure.

options.text: I have visit Cusco twice.
options.feedback: After 'have' the verb must be the past participle 'visited'.

options.text: I visited have Cusco twice.
options.feedback: The verb order is broken in this sentence.

options.text: I am visit Cusco twice.
options.feedback: An auxiliary plus a bare verb is not a valid combination.

questions.explanation:
'I have visited Cusco' combina correctamente el auxiliar 'have' con el participio 'visited'.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete: '____ you ever eaten ceviche?'

options.text: Did
options.feedback: 'Did you ever eat...?' asks about a finished past event.

options.text: Have
options.feedback: 'Have you ever eaten...?' is the standard present perfect question.

options.text: Do
options.feedback: 'Do you ever eat...?' speaks about a habit, not about experience.

options.text: Are
options.feedback: 'Are' cannot be followed by the participle 'eaten'.

questions.explanation:
Las preguntas de experiencia se forman con 'have' mas participio y el marcador 'ever'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What is the difference between 'I have been to Lima' and 'I have gone to Lima'?

options.text: Both mean the speaker is currently in Lima
options.feedback: Only 'have gone' places the speaker in Lima at the time of speaking.

options.text: Both refer to a future plan
options.feedback: Both forms concern the past in relation to the present.

options.text: 'Have been' is the simple past of 'be'
options.feedback: 'Have been' is a present perfect form.

options.text: 'Have been' is experience; 'have gone' means the person is there now
options.feedback: The difference lies in whether the speaker returned.

questions.explanation:
'Have been' indica experiencia sin precisar si se sigue alli; 'have gone' indica que la persona esta alli ahora.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Look at the sentence: 'I have saw that documentary twice.' What is the error?

options.text: 'Saw' must be the participle 'seen'
options.feedback: After 'have' the past participle is required.

options.text: Nothing is wrong with the sentence
options.feedback: Using the simple past form after 'have' is a clear error.

options.text: 'Twice' must be 'two times' only
options.feedback: 'Twice' is the correct short adverb for two occurrences.

options.text: 'Documentary' must be plural
options.feedback: The singular form agrees with 'that documentary'.

questions.explanation:
El participio de 'see' es 'seen'; 'saw' es el pasado simple y no puede usarse con 'have'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which time expression normally goes with the present perfect?

options.text: yesterday
options.feedback: 'Yesterday' is a finished past marker and requires the simple past.

options.text: just
options.feedback: 'Just' is a present perfect marker: 'She has just arrived'.

options.text: last night
options.feedback: 'Last night' is a completed past period and goes with the past simple.
A specific past year requires the simple past tense.

questions.explanation:
'Already', 'just', 'yet', 'ever' y 'never' son marcadores del presente perfecto. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the dialogue: 'A: Have you ever been to the Sacred Valley? B: Yes, I ____ there in 2018.'

options.text: have gone
options.feedback: The present perfect is incompatible with a finished past year.

options.text: am going
options.feedback: The present continuous places the action now, not in 2018.

options.text: went
options.feedback: 'Went' is the simple past required by the closed past time 'in 2018'.

options.text: had gone
options.feedback: The past perfect would require another past reference point.

questions.explanation:
Como 'in 2018' es un tiempo cerrado, la respuesta va en pasado simple: 'went'. Conviene practicarlo con otros ejemplos antes del examen.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence forms the present perfect correctly?

options.text: They have already submit the forms.
options.feedback: The participle 'submitted' is required after 'have'.

options.text: They already have submit the forms.
options.feedback: The adverb must sit between the auxiliary and the participle.

options.text: They have already submitted the forms.
options.feedback: Auxiliary 'have' plus participle with the marker 'already'.

options.text: They are already submitted the forms.
options.feedback: 'Are' plus participle is not a valid combination here.

questions.explanation:
Solo la forma con 'have' mas participio y sujeto plural construye correctamente el presente perfecto.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What does the present perfect express in 'I have lost my passport'?

options.text: A repeated action in the past
options.feedback: Repetition would need 'twice' or a frequency adverb.

options.text: A future intention
options.feedback: No future element appears in the sentence.

options.text: A past action with a present result
options.feedback: That present relevance is the core meaning of the present perfect.

options.text: A habit that continues indefinitely
options.feedback: A habit belongs to the simple present.

questions.explanation:
La forma conecta una accion pasada con una consecuencia que sigue vigente en el presente.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct negative form of the present perfect.

options.text: She not has arrived yet.
options.feedback: The auxiliary must precede the adverb 'not'.

options.text: She has not arrive yet.
options.feedback: The participle 'arrived' is required after 'has not'.

options.text: She does not arrived yet.
options.feedback: The present perfect requires 'has not', not 'does not'.

options.text: She has not arrived yet.
options.feedback: 'Has not' plus participle is the correct negative structure.

questions.explanation:
La negacion combina 'have/has not' con el participio del verbo. Este matiz se comprueba comparando con el resto de opciones.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'He ____ in Cusco ____ he was a child.'

options.text: lived / since
options.feedback: The simple past would contradict the continuing meaning implied by 'since'.

options.text: has lived / since
options.feedback: 'Has lived since' expresses a situation that began in the past and continues.

options.text: has living / since
options.feedback: After 'has' the participle 'lived' is required, not the gerund.

options.text: is living / since
options.feedback: The present continuous cannot be combined with 'since' in this usage.

questions.explanation:
'Since' introduce un punto de partida en el pasado y por eso se usa con el presente perfecto.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly uses the present perfect progressive?

options.text: She is learning English for two years.
options.feedback: The present continuous is not normally used with a completed duration.

options.text: She learns English for two years.
options.feedback: The simple present with 'for' describes a habit, not an ongoing duration.

options.text: She had learned English for two years.
options.feedback: The past perfect places the learning before another past moment.

options.text: She has been learning English for two years.
options.feedback: 'Has been learning' marks a duration started in the past and still ongoing.

questions.explanation:
'Have been' mas gerundio describe una accion que empezo en el pasado y continua. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read: 'Historians still debate why the empire declined.' What does the sentence tell us?

options.text: The debate began in the past and continues now
options.feedback: 'Still' connects an earlier situation with the present moment.

options.text: The debate finished recently
options.feedback: 'Still' is the opposite of a completed action.

options.text: The debate has not started yet
options.feedback: 'Still' presupposes that the debate is already under way.

options.text: Historians agree on the explanation
options.feedback: 'Debate' signals disagreement, the opposite of agreement.

questions.explanation:
'Still' indica que el debate continua desde el pasado hasta el presente. Conviene practicarlo con otros ejemplos antes del examen.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence uses 'yet' correctly?

options.text: He has not yet found his keys.
options.feedback: This placement is also accepted, but the sentence contradicts the 'end position' rule used here.

options.text: He has not found his keys yet.
options.feedback: The adverb 'yet' at the end of the negative sentence is the standard position.

options.text: He yet has not found his keys.
options.feedback: Putting 'yet' before the auxiliary is not the natural order.

options.text: Yet he has not found his keys.
options.feedback: 'Yet' cannot open the sentence in this meaning.

questions.explanation:
En afirmativas y negativas 'yet' suele ir al final de la oracion. Este matiz se comprueba comparando con el resto de opciones.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What is the question form with 'how many times'?

options.text: How many times did you go to Lima?
options.feedback: That asks about past occurrences with a closed time reference.

options.text: How many times have you been to Lima?
options.feedback: 'Have you been' is the correct structure for counting experiences.

options.text: How many times you have been to Lima?
options.feedback: The auxiliary is missing before the subject.

options.text: How many times are you been to Lima?
options.feedback: 'Are' cannot be combined with the participle 'been'.

questions.explanation:
La pregunta sobre numero de veces en presente perfecto usa 'have' mas participio. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence is NOT correct?

options.text: I have visited Lima last Tuesday.
options.feedback: A closed past time requires the simple past: 'I visited Lima last Tuesday'.

options.text: She has gone to Cusco twice.
options.feedback: A counted experience with 'twice' is correct in the present perfect.

options.text: We have known each other since 2010.
options.feedback: 'Since' plus a date is a standard present perfect pattern.

options.text: They have just arrived at the airport.
options.feedback: 'Just' is a present perfect marker, so the form is correct.

questions.explanation:
El presente perfecto es incompatible con una fecha cerrada como 'last Tuesday'. Conviene practicarlo con otros ejemplos antes del examen.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the best correction for: 'She have worked here for five years.'

options.text: She are working here for five years.
options.feedback: 'Are' does not agree with 'she', and the continuous is wrong with the duration.

options.text: She have been working here since five years.
options.feedback: The auxiliary is wrong and 'since' cannot be followed by a duration.

options.text: She works here for five years.
options.feedback: The simple present would describe a job, not an accumulated duration.

options.text: She has worked here for five years.
options.feedback: 'Has' agrees with the third person singular subject 'she'.

questions.explanation:
El sujeto 'she' es tercera persona singular, por lo que el auxiliar debe ser 'has'. Este matiz se comprueba comparando con el resto de opciones.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read the sentence: 'By next year the city will have built two more hospitals.' What does the sentence describe?

options.text: Hospitals that will start next year
options.feedback: The sentence speaks of completion, not of the start of works.

options.text: Hospitals that already exist
options.feedback: The completion lies in the future, not in the past.

options.text: Hospitals that will be finished before next year
options.feedback: The future perfect places the completion ahead of the deadline.

options.text: A hospital that will be demolished
options.feedback: Nothing in the sentence refers to demolition.

questions.explanation:
Aunque el enunciado usa futuro perfecto, remite a una accion que estara completada antes de ese momento.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which statement about the present perfect is correct?

options.text: It refers only to actions with a specific date
options.feedback: A specific date excludes the present perfect and requires the simple past.

options.text: It is used only in questions
options.feedback: It appears in statements as well as in questions.

options.text: It describes habits that never change
options.feedback: Habits belong to the simple present.

options.text: It links a past action to a present situation
options.feedback: That present relevance is exactly what the form expresses.

questions.explanation:
El presente perfecto vincula una accion pasada con una situacion o resultado presente.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete: 'They ____ for the bus for twenty minutes.'

options.text: are waiting
options.feedback: The present continuous is possible in a narrow sense but not with the standard duration reading.

options.text: waited
options.feedback: The simple past would not indicate that they are still waiting.

options.text: have been waiting
options.feedback: 'Have been waiting' plus 'for' expresses a duration continuing to the present.

options.text: will wait
options.feedback: The future refers to an action not yet begun.

questions.explanation:
La duracion con 'for' y la continuacion en el presente exigen presente perfecto. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What does 'I have known him since childhood' imply?

options.text: The acquaintance began in childhood and still holds
options.feedback: 'Since childhood' plus the present perfect marks an ongoing relationship.

options.text: The acquaintance ended in childhood
options.feedback: Ending the relationship would require the simple past.

options.text: The acquaintance will begin in childhood
options.feedback: Childhood is a past reference, not a future one.

options.text: The speaker met him yesterday
options.feedback: The sentence places the origin of the relationship much earlier.

questions.explanation:
La expresion indica una relacion que se inicia en la infancia y que sigue vigente. Conviene practicarlo con otros ejemplos antes del examen.
